question: Should OpenClaw define a general outbound agent-attestation security contract, or limit any future solution to a specifically scoped plugin/provider integration until a trusted issuer and privacy model exist?
rationale: The requested cryptographic claim changes what third parties may trust about user-controlled agent traffic; code review cannot safely choose its issuer, guarantee, identity fields, replay policy, or egress scope without maintainer intent.

options.title: Define a narrow core contract
options.body: Approve a documented attestation guarantee, issuer/verifier model, allowlisted audience rules, and a deliberately bounded set of supported egress paths before implementation.

options.title: Keep this plugin-scoped
options.body: Require the requesting service or plugin to own its own authentication and consent flow unless it demonstrates a missing generic OpenClaw extension seam.

options.title: Decline agent-origin claims
options.body: Keep ordinary service authentication as the supported model and do not expose a first-party claim that a request was made by an agent.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow core contract
recommendation.body: Approve a documented attestation guarantee, issuer/verifier model, allowlisted audience rules, and a deliberately bounded set of supported egress paths before implementation.
